prerequisites: Recommended: competencies taught in the modules Logic, Object-oriented Programming, Algorithms and Data Structures, and basic knowledge in functional programming (e.g. in Scala, Haskell or Python).

learning_outcomes.text: Students can deploy and apply current research tools.
Students can independently explore new application areas.
Students can explain concepts of software verification and synthesis.
Students can discuss the application and limits of decision procedures.
Students can explain the theory and application of lambda calculus.

syllabus_topics: Practical verification and synthesis of Scala programs with "Leon" and their theoretical backgrounds:
Hoare Calculus, Verification Conditions, Weakest Preconditions
Decision Procedures (Linear Arithmetic, Abstract Data Types, Quantifier Elimination)
Combination of Decision Procedures (Satisfiability Modulo Theories and Z3)
Lambda Expressions in Scala and Java 8
Modeling and Verification of Functional Languages (Leon)

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercises tasks (at least 50 percent of points)
Oral presentation of solutions to at least two exercise tasks

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise tasks and orally present the solution of at least two of the exercise tasks. The final assessment is either a written exam or an oral exam. Grading is done with 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science program.
bibliography: N. Bjørner et. al.: Program Verification as Satisfiability Modulo Theories
R. Blanc et al.: An Overview of the Leon Verification System
M. Gordon: Programming Language Theory and its Implementation. Prentice Hall
